name: gizza-ai/python-syntax-check
summary: Check Python 3 syntax and pinpoint the error line and column

tool.description: Check pasted Python 3 source for compile-time syntax errors without running it. Reports the first SyntaxError, IndentationError or TabError with its line, column, message and a caret-marked echo of the offending line, plus optional hints that translate Python-2-only constructs into Python 3. Supports CPython's module, expression and interactive compile modes, text or JSON output, a filename label, and input line/character stats. Runtime errors, code execution and PEP 8 style linting are deliberately out of scope.

code.description: Python source code to check. It is parsed with the Python 3 grammar and never executed, so runtime errors such as NameError are out of scope.

mode.description: Which of CPython's compile() modes to parse with: module for a whole file, expression for a single expression as eval() accepts, interactive for a REPL-style block.

format.description: Output format: a human-readable compiler-style report, or JSON diagnostics for scripts and CI.

show_context.description: Echo the offending source line with a ^ caret under the exact column, the way a Python traceback does. Default on.

python2_hints.description: Explain Python-2-only constructs (print statement, except E comma name, raise E comma msg, exec statement, <>, backtick repr, 0755 octal) in Python 3 terms. Default on.

stats.description: Include the input size summary: total lines, non-empty lines and characters. Default on.

filename.description: Label used in the report, so output reads like a real compiler line, for example app.py:12:5. Defaults to <input>.
